data.content_ref: inline:Define a staged grounded extension parameterized by a discrete clock t: at each stage, suspended nodes may be reopened only if a fresh edge-construction warrant was committed in the previous stage, and the extension is the limit of the stage sequence. This makes suspension a dynamic, revisable state rather than a terminal label, and preserves determinism per stage. The criticism: the limit may not be reached in polynomial time unless the stage count is bounded a priori, and the monotonicity of the sequence across stages (reopening is not monotone) breaks the fixed-point determinism guarantee.
